title: Narrative Structure Recognition
summary: Teach the reviewer to understand how events function within the structure of the screenplay before evaluating any potential violation.

definitions.scenePurpose: The role a scene plays in advancing the story.
definitions.characterArc: The evolution of a character across the screenplay.
definitions.storyArc: The overall progression of the narrative.
definitions.turningPoint: An event that significantly changes the direction of the story.

reviewerPrinciples: Review the scene as part of the story.
A scene may intentionally create tension without endorsing harmful behaviour.
Character growth often changes the meaning of earlier actions.
reviewerQuestions: What is the purpose of this scene?
Does this scene establish, escalate or resolve conflict?
Is this behaviour later condemned or rewarded?
Would the story lose meaning if this scene were removed?

decisionTree.question: Has the narrative role of the scene been identified?
Does later story context change the interpretation?

examples.text: The villain threatens the hero early in the story.
The villain is arrested at the end.

questions.question: Should scenes be reviewed independently from the story?
Can later scenes change the interpretation of earlier scenes?
